newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Budget Committee sets economic hearings.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Budget Committee sets economic hearings.

text.p: The Senate Budget Committee has set two economic hearings in the new year, including Jan 21 testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the state of the U.S. economy, a committee aide said Wednesday.
Congressional Budget Office Director June O'Neill was scheduled to testify Jan 28 at a hearing on the CBO's economic and budget outlook.
Other hearings, including hearings on President Clinton's budget, were not yet confirmed.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was tentatively scheduled to testify at a possible Feb 4 hearing on revenue proposals in the president's 1998 budget, a draft schedule showed.
Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines was tentatively scheduled to testify at a possible Feb 5 hearing on the president's 1998 budget.
Other possible hearings, not yet confirmed, may be held on the consumer price index, long-term budget projections, Medicare, and Social Security reform proposals.
